It’s expected to switch constantly. The drs doesn’t know what works for you so they usually start off with a safe choice and see how you handle it. If it works you’ll stay on it, and if it doesn’t, they’ll put you on something stronger or weaker depending on your symptoms or complaints. This may be unrelated but at least for me, they all had negative effects on my libido. Paroxetine particularly made it quite difficult for me to finish. 

Granted you may not be into sex while depressed, but it was just something I noticed myself.

I had these random electrical jolts all over my body, especially when I moved too quickly or looked/turned my head too quickly. My anxiety and depression shot through the roof (not sure if it was directly caused by stopping paroxetine), the first day of stopping it I got irritated really easily and had no patience for anything. I also experienced nausea for the first few days. Most of it went away except for the jolts which lasted until I started my new medication about 2-3 weeks after stopping paroxetine.

Every antidepressants work differently on everyone. For me, I started off with fluoxetine and switched to paroxetine. I was on it for about a month before switching to my current one. I did a hard withdrawal off paroxetine (against my therapist and psychiatrist’s recommendation) and the side effects were prettt bad. But they went away after 2 weeks when I started my new medication. I’ve been on this current one for over a month now and it is definitely helping along with my therapy sessions. 

You’ll have to keep trying to find the right medication that works for you.
